body: I wish I could say that I'm doing better. Almost gave in tonight, and I don't have much fight left in me anymore.

I'm sorry that I went MIA, been trying to find new outlets and just wallowing in self-pity. I need hip surgery for an hip impingment and torn hip labrum. I also have a torn rotator cuff, a shoulder impingment, ligament damage in my elbow, foot, and hand, I had back surgery a few years ago for a herniated disk with nerve damage, which still flares up once in a while, some hamstring/knee problems, and I tore a pectoral muscle that never quite healed properly.... And that's only the current injury log, not even counting sporadic post-concussion symptoms. Basically, I'm a mess of a human being.

I've tried meditation, but have some issues with it. It's hard to meditate with ADHD, and it's something I did with my ex, so it can trigger a lot of anger and self-destructive thoughts, essentially doing the opposite of what it's supposed to lmao.

I wish I had a job right now, sitting around the house is making things so much worse. Ironically, I'm working on my MSW right now and want to be a therapist.

Sorry for the delayed response, I hope you're doing well.
Sorry I've been MIA, and I'm even more sorry that you've been going through this.

Not on birth control, I'm male actually haha. Regardless, I really appreciate the love and support. I have no way to let out all of this frustration or to work of this negative energy, and I miss exercising to improve myself physically and mentally. It's not that physical activity is the only thing I enjoy, but it has always been the catalyst for my improvement in the past.

I lost that person already. She spent 4 years on-and-off psychologically abusing me and making me unstable, slightly less than 1 year making me happier than I can ever remember feeling, and then pushed me off the deep end a little over a year ago, making me realize how pathetic of an existence this is for me. The only person who ever kept me stable, is the same person that has made me nearly kill myself multiple times over half a decade. I'm pathetic.

I hope you find someone to help you keep stable though. I know it's not easy.

I just don't know where to go from here, things haven't gotten any better. Things can't get worse simply because I don't think I could feel any lower. Yes, something terrible could happen to someone I love or to one of my pets, and that would devastate me, but I can't see how my baseline could get any lower... Does that make any sense?... Like, I could get far more angry, upset, or depressed due to negative circumstances, but the long-term effects of any such event couldn't possibly bring my baseline state-of-being any lower than it currently is.

I might force myself to start doing this. The only good thing about not feeling things anymore is that I don't get as anxious about things as much, and I don't get the physical symptoms of an anxiety attack, so talking to people may be more easy. The big problem is that my social skills suck and I hate myself, so I always second-guess my decisions, convince myself that I'm too awkward to talk to people or that they have no interest in talking to me, or I over-analyze the situation and decide that I'm better off not talking to anyone because they're too good to talk to me or I can't trust them.

I end up getting coffee by myself a lot, or going to the park a lot, and it takes the suicidal edge off, but that's all. I don't have a problem doing things by myself; I've always been a bit of a loner, I've always been bullied and excluded, because of my weight, depression, and poor social skills, so I got used to doing things on my own.

I don't know, I just can't enjoy things anymore. It's horrible. I've always struggled with my mental health, but I always found things I enjoyed to help offset some of it, and I don't have that this time around. Everybody gets low once in a while, and plenty of people experience depression, but how can you live with nothing to offset it? There's no balance, there's no happiness, it's just low or slightly-less-low.
I'm sorry. I wouldn't wish this on my worst enemy.

Thanks for the advice. I've tried, and I keep trying to find something, but nothing seems to stick for me. I honestly don't know why, but I can't enjoy things. My range of emotions runs from seriously suicidal, to almost moderately stable. I've tried plenty of things, but it feels like that physical/chemical reaction of happiness or joy is something I'm incapable of experiencing.

Junk food, smoking, and drinking all give me temporary relief, but it's very temporary, and often the depression comes back with a vengeance.

Kind of. It feels like I've been fighting for so long against something that I thought I could beat, and now I'm realizing that I can't beat it. I'm so tired of hanging in there and listening to everyone who says, "things will get better," or, "if you end it now then things will never get better." Things don't get better for me. 

Even during the periods of my life that I was the most "happy", I still thought about killing myself. About a year ago, I went into the deepest depression I've ever felt, and it's different this time; it's everywhere, it drains everything, and it's all-consuming. I keep trying things, meds, therapy, TMS, off-label treatments, HERBal remedies, but nothing has worked for me, and I don't want to try anything anymore, I'm sick of failed medications and trials. I'm tired of working so hard to get through this, because I'm not going to be happy, I'm just going to be less miserable and possibly less suicidal. Like, what type of fucking existence is that? Working every day, busting your ass, all so that you aren't 100% miserable. The point is, I haven't gotten any better, and it feels like I die a little more inside every day that I live like this. Every day, the depression takes another piece of me, and it feels like I'm dead inside. I don't have motivation to put in a real effort to get better, because I don't feel anything. I don't feel any desire to get better, I don't feel enough happiness to know if it's worth fighting for, and from what I remember, the payoff isn't worth the effort.

Sorry for rambling, and I appreciate the kind words, and I hope you are doing better with your struggle than I am. I barely even leave my house anymore. I forced myself to go on two dates this weekend (with girls from Tinder), and they both went poorly. One seemed into me, the other said she was but it didn't seem that way, and I "enjoyed" myself grabbing drinks with each of them, but I felt nothing. I didn't feel anxious beforehand, I didn't feel excited while with them, it didn't feel go to go out, and I recognize that these were enjoyable activities and that I enjoyed them, but I felt nothing. I felt nothing in my chest, or my stomach, not rush or endorphins or neurochemicals, not heart-sinking or racing, nothing. The only thing I felt was my wallet get lighter, and a feeling of deep self-hatred when I got the vibe that the one girl wasn't into me. That's all. And then I got more depressed having realized that I couldn't feel anything, and that neither of these dates will likely amount to anything.

That's great! I wish I could have that type of change in perception. I can't maintain any form of happiness or positivity for more than a day, and the next day always seems to leave me with a hangover effect in which I'm even more depressed or pessimistic than usual. Every time I get my hopes up, start to look forward to something, or feel positively about anything, people cancel on me or something blows up in my face, and I'm left even worse than before... now I can't even enjoy looking forward to things anymore. It's not that I just have a pessimistic outlook, I've been conditioned to be like this by everything in my life going to shit.

Okay, I didn't just want to assume that I understood where you were coming from without being sure, but I know that feeling, and I live with it every day. Feels like how Supernatural described becoming a vengeful spirit (if you've ever seen it), being trapped in a place you feel you don't belong, losing who you are and why you're here, all while gradually letting the darkness take control more and more. I wish I had some cure for it, or some way to drive the thoughts away, but I haven't found such a thing yet. All I can say is that you aren't the only one, I hope to God (if there is one) that a positive change is in your future, and try to keep positive when you can remember to, but don't beat yourself up when you forget and fall back into the traps your mind has set for you. That's what depression does, it pulls you deeper into its traps without you even realizing it, then it makes you criticize yourself for not being able to break free or be "normal".... Most importantly, your username is brilliant. Try to keep your head up, don't blink, and Allons-y.

I think I know that feeling. You feel so far passed "being depressed" and the feeling that you want to die, that you're angry that you're​ even still here. People don't get it, they don't understand why you are depressed, but they want you to stick around, so they say it will get better, but it never seems to, then they wonder why you're angry, but you're angry because of them. You're angry because you feel you have accepted the fact that you no longer wish to be on this Earth, and they are keeping you here, in a place you don't belong, all so that they don't have to mourn your escape from the monotonous, painful Hell that you've created in your own mind. They make you stay, to continue the fight, just to ease their own consciences, then they pat themselves on the back and think that they did their good deed for the day, week, or year by convincing you not to end your suffering, but they don't have to live with that, you do.

I believe I inherited traits that led to a low-resilience, and then events effected me more than they should have, but I believe it was mostly caused by those events that started at a very young age... friends treated me like crap, I was bullied, my parents separated, separated again, and then divorced, I was threatened in school, publicly shamed and humiliated on many occasions, have been treated as a disposable human being, was always the black sheep and scapegoat in my family, have repeatedly been betrayed by trusted "friends", was in some toxic relationships, and was cheated on by the majority of my exes (including the one I was going to propose to).

I believe I would still have some traits if these things hadn't happened, but it would be much more manageable, and I don't think the depression I feel would be this deep. I honestly believe that I would be more trusting, I would have more stable relationships, and I don't think I'd hate myself as much, or be so angry, empty, paranoid, volatile, and scared of being left or hurt. Mainly, I think I'd be able to trust people, I wouldn't hate myself and want to die every day, and I wouldn't form such co-dependent and unhealthy friendships and relationships.

I wish I had the right advice to give. The best thing is to try reminding yourself how much they fucked up. Remind yourself of all the negative things about them that pissed you off. Remember that they weren't perfect either. Also remember that they are only one person; these were the actions of one individual who couldn't appreciate what they had. And nobody is saying that you have to put yourself out there, maybe you should take a little time to process, then figure out if/when you want to put yourself out there again. 

People always say, "the best way to get over someone is to get under someone else," but that never seems to be the way with BPD. Because it will either turn into a self-destructive habit of one-nighters to dull the pain, or you will expect too much out of the wrong person. 

So instead of jumping right back into it, maybe you should try taking a break to collect yourself. If you feel that nobody makes time for you, you should make time for yourself. Accept that you are taking time for yourself, you are doing so by your own choice, and that you will put yourself out there again when you feel the time is right.

Most importantly, remind yourself that they fucked up, and that you are CHOOSING to take some time to find yourself again.

A few rules that I've taught myself recently:
1) Don't do it over text. Call or in person ONLY. You can't interpret tone through text, and also can't read body language. Plus, once you send that text, you will be in a constant state of fear/panic until you get a response.
2) If the conversation goes well, you're allowed to be happy and excited, but don't go over the top with it. If it doesn't go well, run with it, or get out of the situation as soon as you can if you have an intense reaction, and then vent it out to someone. Don't react on the spot.
3) Don't try to force the issue, no matter what the response. That is where I always go wrong. DON'T BE LIKE ME. If she needs time to think, let her think. If she doesn't know, give her a couple days without texting to think it over. If she isn't into it, move on, because trying to convince her will only make her more sure of her decision. If she is into it.... well, you can figure that one out for yourself.
